drug_class: Anti-CD19 monoclonal antibody (a type of targeted biologic therapy)
purpose: Inebilizumab-Cdon is used to treat adults with a rare condition called neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, or NMOSD, especially in people who have a specific antibody called AQP4-IgG in their blood. This disease can cause serious problems with your vision and movement. This medicine helps reduce the number of attacks or flare-ups caused by the disease.
how_it_works: Your immune system has certain cells called B cells that play a big role in causing the inflammation that damages your nerves in NMOSD. This medicine works like a smart missile — it finds and destroys those B cells by targeting a protein called CD19 on their surface. By reducing these harmful B cells, the medicine helps calm down the immune system attack on your nerves and spinal cord.
common_side_effects: Urinary tract infections (bladder infections), joint pain, infusion reactions during or shortly after the IV treatment (like flushing, headache, nausea, or dizziness), back pain, and low levels of certain immune cells in your blood.
warnings: Because this medicine lowers your immune system, you may get infections more easily, including serious ones. Make sure all your vaccines are up to date before starting treatment. Tell your doctor right away if you have signs of infection like fever or chills. This medicine should not be given if you have an active infection. It can also lower immunoglobulin levels over time, which are proteins that help fight infection. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should talk to their doctor, as this medicine may affect the baby.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) in a clinic or hospital — not taken as a pill at home. The usual starting dose involves two infusions given about 2 weeks apart. After that, you receive one infusion every 6 months to keep the disease under control. Each infusion typically takes about 90 minutes, and you will be monitored for reactions during and after the infusion.
